categories.description: Labels things incorrectly or sees things that aren't there.

sub_categories.description: Inventing arbitrary values or information not grounded in the problem.
Ignoring clearly stated or observable data (e.g., total domino count, timestamps).

categories.description: Problems with thinking process and conclusions.

sub_categories.description: Early mistake keeps getting carried forward
Comes up with a wrong premise to solve the problem.
Misunderstanding the task goal
Misinterpreting key terms.

categories.description: Mistakes in indexing, distance calculation, or arithmetic derived from prior reasoning failures.

sub_categories.description: Applying numerical data incorrectly (e.g., using signed differences instead of absolute values).
Does a mathematical operation incorrectly.
Counts too many or too few cubes/faces/etc.

categories.description: Mistakes in interpreting time-based sequences, dynamics, or ordering of events.

sub_categories.description: Incorrectly identifies the timestamp at which an event occurs.
Doesn't include all of the important events of the sequence mentioned in the ground truth.
Misidentifies where the trajectory starts.
Mixes up the order of events

categories.description: Errors stemming from incorrect interpretation of visual content or conflating interface elements with actual data.

sub_categories.description: Mistaking visual elements (e.g., color palette for actual domino sequence).
Focusing on the legend elements instead of the main content.
Incorrectly identifying shape type, color, or presence compared to ground truth.
Making assumptions about visuals without relying on explicit descriptors.
Incorrectly identifying the index of a target element (not correct using 0-based indexing nor 1-based indexing).
Guesses wrong dimensions (e.g. 3×3×3 instead of 4×5×5)
Doesn't accurately describe the object's structure
Doesn't see which cubes were removed
Doesn't Recognize Hidden Faces
Calls a shape the wrong name (e.g. calls a square in the video a circle).
